section: Perspectives in Education · Ch16 — RTE Act 2009
subject: Perspectives in Education
stem: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 guarantees free and compulsory education to every child of the age group:

options.option_text: 6 to 14 years
3 to 14 years
6 to 18 years
5 to 15 years

explanation: The RTE Act operationalises Article 21-A, covering children aged 6–14 years (elementary education, Classes I–VIII). Pre-school (3–6) is encouraged but not the Act's core guarantee.

section: Perspectives in Education · Ch16 — RTE Act 2009
subject: Perspectives in Education
stem: The RTE Act, 2009 gives effect to which Article inserted by the 86th Constitutional Amendment?

options.option_text: Article 21-A
Article 45
Article 29
Article 15

explanation: The 86th Amendment (2002) inserted Article 21-A making elementary education a Fundamental Right; the RTE Act, 2009 is its enabling legislation. Article 45 (a Directive Principle) now covers early-childhood care below age 6.

section: Perspectives in Education · Ch16 — RTE Act 2009
subject: Perspectives in Education
stem: Under Section 12(1)(c) of the RTE Act, private unaided schools must admit, in Class I, children from disadvantaged and weaker sections to the extent of at least:

options.option_text: 25 percent of the strength of that class
10 percent of the strength of that class
50 percent of the strength of that class
15 percent of the strength of that class

explanation: Section 12(1)(c) mandates a 25% reservation in entry-level class in private unaided schools for disadvantaged and economically weaker-section children, with the State reimbursing costs.

section: Perspectives in Education · Ch16 — RTE Act 2009
subject: Perspectives in Education
stem: Which of the following is expressly prohibited by the RTE Act, 2009?

options.option_text: Physical punishment and mental harassment of children
Continuous and comprehensive evaluation
Admission of a child without an age proof
Free textbooks to children in government schools

explanation: Section 17 bars physical punishment and mental harassment. The Act, conversely, mandates CCE, forbids denying admission for lack of age proof, and provides free textbooks.

section: Perspectives in Education · Ch16 — RTE Act 2009
subject: Perspectives in Education
stem: As originally enacted, Section 16 of the RTE Act provided that no child admitted to a school shall be:

options.option_text: Held back in any class or expelled till completion of elementary education
Given any form of continuous assessment
Admitted after the age of eight years under any circumstance
Taught in the mother tongue as medium of instruction

explanation: Section 16 originally embodied the 'no-detention policy' up to Class VIII. (The 2019 amendment later allowed States to hold a regular exam in Classes V and VIII with one re-exam.) The Act encourages mother tongue and mandates assessment, and out-of-school children may be admitted age-appropriately.

section: Perspectives in Education · Ch16 — RTE Act 2009
subject: Perspectives in Education
stem: Under the RTE Act, the School Management Committee (SMC) of a government/aided school must have at least what proportion of members from among parents/guardians, and what proportion of women?

options.option_text: 75% parents/guardians, and 50% women
50% parents/guardians, and 25% women
100% parents/guardians, and 33% women
60% teachers, and 40% women

explanation: Section 21 requires SMCs constituted with three-fourths (75%) members being parents/guardians (with proportionate representation of disadvantaged groups), and 50% of members being women.

section: Perspectives in Education · Ch16 — RTE Act 2009
subject: Perspectives in Education
stem: The RTE Act's Schedule prescribes a pupil-teacher ratio for primary classes (I–V) of:
explanation: The RTE norms specify a PTR of 30:1 at the primary level (I–V) and 35:1 at the upper-primary level (VI–VIII).

section: Perspectives in Education · Ch16 — RTE Act 2009
subject: Perspectives in Education
stem: The requirement that a person must pass a Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) to be eligible for appointment as a teacher flows from which authority under the RTE Act?

options.option_text: The minimum qualifications laid down by the academic authority (NCTE)
A direct provision of Article 21-A itself
The State Public Service Commission rules only
The Finance Commission recommendations

explanation: Section 23 empowers the Central Government to notify the academic authority (NCTE) that lays down minimum teacher qualifications; NCTE made passing the TET a mandatory qualification.
